messages.author: 9f45b22254c8c1da
messages.subject: Negative intercepts for latent factors
parts:
Hi, 

I conducted a multi-group CFA (N1 = 489, N2 = 434) using this six-factor model: 

pers_model1 <- ' 
    neg_act =~ PERS_2 + PERS_8 + PERS_14 + PERS_20 + PERS_26
    neg_int =~ PERS_6 + PERS_12 + PERS_18 + PERS_24 + PERS_30
    neg_dur =~ PERS_4 + PERS_10 + PERS_16 + PERS_22 + PERS_28
    pos_act =~ PERS_1 + PERS_7 + PERS_13 + PERS_19 + PERS_25
    pos_int =~ PERS_5 + PERS_11 + PERS_17 + PERS_23 + PERS_29
    pos_dur =~ PERS_3 + PERS_9 + PERS_15 + PERS_21 + PERS_27'

I was testing for partial scalar invariance when I noticed that the intercept estimates for the latent factors of group 2 were negative. I also noted that the confidence intervals included 0. Is this an issue? In addition, I noticed that lavaan only calculated the intercept estimates for group 2, and not group 1. Is this normal as well? 

Thank you.
Joan

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: Negative intercepts for latent factors
parts:
The usual default in multiple-group CFA is to constrain the latent-variable intercepts (same as means if exogenous) to zero in one group and freely estimate them in other groups. So negative values in group 2, all else being equal, indicates the means are lower than in group 1 (on a metric untethered from the original indicators). Confidence intervals including aero suggest they're not significantly lower.

So this is all quite ordinary.
